title: Intel Moves Forward at Ohio One With First Major Structural Truss Installation Arizona Fab 62 Tooling
gist: Intel installed the first major structural truss on the first fab at its Ohio One site, while tool installation has begun at Arizona Fab 62. Ohio timelines have slipped to 2030-2031 for the first fab, and the author frames the open question as whether Intel can build fabs that customers fill fast enough.

themes.theme: Ohio One construction milestone and delays

insights.claim: Intel installed the first major structural truss for the first fab at its Ohio One site in New Albany, Ohio, a visible construction milestone.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Physical progress at Ohio is still early-stage; shells, tools and wafer starts remain ahead.
insights.locator: Intel has reached a visible construction milestone

insights.claim: Ohio One was announced in January 2022 with production targeted for 2025 on a 1,000-acre site east of Columbus.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Provides the baseline against which the Ohio delay is measured.
insights.locator: The Ohio One project was announced in January 2022

insights.claim: In a February 2025 report to the Ohio Department of Development, Intel projected finishing construction of the first Ohio fab in 2030 with operations in 2030-2031, and the second fab finishing in 2031 with operations in 2032.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Ohio capacity contributes nothing to Intel Foundry volume until the 2030s, so near-term foundry thesis rests elsewhere.
insights.locator: Construction timelines have shifted since the initial announcement.

insights.claim: The author cautions that completing shells, installing and calibrating equipment, and running wafers are all non-trivial steps, so Ohio is still early days for those tracking the foundry business.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Execution risk remains large; treat construction photos as weak evidence of foundry competitiveness.
insights.locator: For readers tracking the foundry business

themes.theme: CHIPS Act funding and Intel's US footprint

insights.claim: In March 2024 Intel and the White House announced a preliminary memorandum of terms for up to $8.5 billion in direct CHIPS Act funding, plus tax credits and low-interest loans, to support fabs in Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio and Oregon.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Federal support underpins Intel's US capex and is a key variable for its funding capacity.
insights.locator: Intel's US expansion received significant federal backing

insights.claim: Intel and the White House said the CHIPS funding was expected to create about 10,000 Intel jobs and another 20,000 construction jobs.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Employment targets are the policy justification that sustains political support for the subsidies.
insights.locator: Intel and the White House said the funding

insights.claim: Intel says Fab 62 in Arizona, its sixth high-volume manufacturing facility, is still under construction but tool installation has begun, with operations planned by the end of 2028.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Arizona is the nearest-term source of added Intel wafer volume, with tool-in as the next checkpoint.
insights.locator: Intel says that Fab 62 is still under construction

insights.claim: The author describes New Mexico packaging as seen as a big growth driver for Foundry, Oregon as receiving research investment, and Intel as having broken ground on a mask manufacturing facility in Santa Clara, California.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Intel's US build-out is split by function across sites, so packaging may monetize before leading-edge fabs.
insights.locator: New Mexico packaging is seen as a big growth driver for Foundry.

themes.theme: Intel Foundry strategy shifts and demand

insights.claim: In September 2024 Intel restructured its foundry business into an independent subsidiary and announced a multi-year deal with AWS to produce custom chips on Intel 18A.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: AWS on 18A is an anchor external-customer reference for the foundry.
insights.locator: In September 2024, Intel restructured its foundry business

insights.claim: Intel paused projects in Poland and Germany by roughly two years, citing market demand, while reaffirming commitment to US sites including Ohio; the author attributes this to a capital crunch.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Capital constraints forced Intel to prioritize US sites and defer European fabs.
insights.locator: The company also paused projects in Poland and Germany

insights.claim: The author argues that demand for semiconductors on leading process nodes is clearly very healthy now, contrasting with the capital crunch that caused earlier delays.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Strong leading-node demand improves the odds Intel's capacity gets filled, if it can execute.
insights.quote: demand for semiconductors on leading process nodes is clearly very healthy these days
insights.locator: Intel Foundry's broader strategy has evolved

insights.claim: The author frames the central test for Intel as whether it can build fabs that customers fill fast enough, despite financial pressures and strategic pivots.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Customer commitments, not construction progress, are the metric to monitor for Foundry.
insights.quote: Now let us see if they can build fabs that customers fill fast enough.
